note.text: Cameroon’s secondary activities include food processing, wood products, cement and aluminium manufacture. The operation performed determines the sector: growing a crop differs from processing it; felling timber differs from making furniture. Location reflects combinations of materials, power, labour, markets and transport. Industries can create jobs and linkages while also creating waste, emissions or pressure on services.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to connect a manufacturing activity to an input, location factor and possible impact. Builds on: manufacturing and location models. Leads to: guided land-use decisions.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: ALUCAM’s official material identifies its aluminium plant at Edéa. Douala provides a port and market context for industrial links. These examples do not imply every plant uses local minerals or operates at constant output. In a fictional food-processing proposal, reliable crop supply and access to customers matter alongside power, storage and waste management.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Name the actual process, then connect a stated factor to its costs or reliability. Consider an environmental or social effect and the evidence needed to assess it. Do not infer present production statistics from a place name.
